---
title: "Which modeled value marks the pth percentile of a normal distribution?"
---

## Question

Which modeled value marks the pth percentile of a normal distribution?

## Work through it

Express the requested percentile as a probability between 0 and 1; choose justified normal mean and sd; use qnorm to get the threshold.

## Worked example: airquality

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("airquality")
mu <- mean(d$Temp)
sigma <- sd(d$Temp)
result <- ru_apply("normal_percentile", mu=mu, sigma=sigma,
                   prob=.9, assume_normal=TRUE)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(pnorm(result,mu,sigma),.9)))
```

The result is the 90th-percentile cutoff under the chosen normal model. To find the 90th percentile of the recorded temperatures directly, use percentile_cutoff instead.

## Adapt to another question

```r
ru_apply("normal_percentile", mu=your_mean, sigma=your_sd, prob=.9, assume_normal=TRUE)
```

A percentile rank is not interchangeable with the underlying measurement value; specify whether the question asks for a rank or a cutoff.

Check the input conditions with `ru_plan("normal_percentile")` before treating a calculation as an inference.
